item.research_question: How can a unique five-element Co–Cu–Fe–Ni–Zn high entropy alloy thin film be synthesized in a single step to achieve soft magnetic properties with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity, overcoming the challenges of anomalous deposition and phase control in aqueous media?
item.material_system: Co–Cu–Fe–Ni–Zn high entropy alloy (near equi-atomic composition)
item.processing_route: Pulse electrodeposition in aqueous medium at ~45 ºC; optimized parameters: forward ON time 50 ms, OFF time 10 ms, applied potential 1.5 V (potentiostatic mode), using sodium citrate as complexing agent and boric acid as buffer.
item.test_conditions: Room temperature characterization; Magnetic properties measured via Vibrating Sample Magnetometry (VSM) and Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) from 9 to 18 GHz; Microstructure analyzed via FESEM, STEM-EDS, 2D X-ray diffraction, and HRTEM.
key_findings: The fabricated Co–Cu–Fe–Ni–Zn HEA thin films exhibited a saturation magnetization (Ms) of ~82 emu/g.
The films showed a relatively low coercivity (Hc) of 19.5 Oe and a remanent magnetization (Mr) of 1.17%.
The alloy hosts nanocrystalline features with a grain size ranging from ~5 to 20 nm.
The films possess a dual-phase structure consisting of Face Centered Cubic (FCC) and Body Centered Cubic (BCC) phases.
FMR measurements yielded a 4πMs value of ~16,136 Oe, indicating potential for microwave device applications.
The composition was found to be uniform throughout the film with no different chemical compositions in FCC and BCC grains.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the soft magnetic behavior and high saturation magnetization to the crystalline nature of the films (FCC/BCC dual phases) and the high concentration of ferromagnetic elements (Fe, Co, Ni) relative to diamagnetic elements (Cu, Zn). The pulse electrodeposition technique controls the reduction of five metal ions uniformly by managing the local pH, minimizing hydroxide formation, and reducing residual stresses, which facilitates the formation of nanocrystalline grains and twins with low stacking fault energy.
item.limitations: The text notes that the composition of the HEA thin films varies slightly between STEM-EDS (single location) and FESEM-EDS (multiple locations) due to local heterogeneities and length scale differences, though the overall distribution is confirmed to be within the HEA range.
item.future_work: The authors propose that additional tuning of the electrodeposition parameters and the relative composition of the constituent elements can further reduce the coercivity of the thin film.
quotes: The fabricated Co–Cu–Fe–Ni–Zn HEA thin films exhibited high saturation magnetization value of ~ 82 emu/g, relatively low coercivity value of 19.5 Oe and remanent magnetization of 1.17%.
This enhancement in the saturation magnetization is attributed to the addition of Co which has high magnetic moment.
